options: To make the graphs look nice
So that noise does not go into the PID
questions.explain: Motor and frame noise must not reach the PID and the motors: D amplifies noise, and the motors heat up.

questions.q: What is the cost of any filter?
questions.explain: A filter lags behind the signal: more filtering means a slower response.

questions.q: The most effective motor noise filter in Betaflight?
questions.explain: The RPM filter places narrow notches exactly on the frequency of each motor using ESC telemetry.

questions.q: What does the dynamic notch do?
options: Places notches on the peaks of the spectrum
Doubles D at the peak frequency
questions.explain: The dynamic notch tracks frame resonances and whatever else the RPM filter did not catch.

questions.q: The order of the cascade in Betaflight (4.5 and 2025.12)?
options: RPM notches → static notches → LPF1 → dynamic notch
Only LPF, the notches are off by default
questions.explain: In filterGyro() the precise per-motor RPM notches come first (after the LPF2 applied at downsampling), then the static notches and LPF1, and the dynamic notch runs last.

questions.q: The motors are hot after a filter change. What do you do?
options: Raise P to override the noise
Roll back and look at the spectrum
questions.explain: Heat is a sign of noise getting through. Go back to the working state, then analyze.

questions.q: In what order are the gyro filters applied in Betaflight (4.5 and 2025.12)?
options: LPF2 → RPM → static notches → LPF1 → dyn notch
questions.explain: The order from filterGyro() (sensors/gyro_filter_impl.c): LPF2 at downsampling, the RPM notches, the two static notches, LPF1, and the dynamic notch last.

options: Disables the RPM filter and enables a PT3 instead
questions.explain: 100 is the defaults; higher means less filtering and less delay.

options: Motor peaks ≤ 5–10 dB above the floor
The motors are warm, not hot
The gyro LPF below 100 Hz on a 5"
questions.explain: A low LPF “hides” the mechanics at the cost of delay — that is not a criterion but a symptom.

questions.q: The course grader's output for a 5" log. Which conclusion is correct?
questions.fragment:
[FAIL] filters  roll noise after filters: 12.9 (limit <= 4.0 deg/s)
[FAIL] filters  roll noise reduction: 4.4 (limit >= 6.0 dB)
[PASS] filters  roll dominant noise frequency: 250.0
[FAIL] rpm      eRPM telemetry logged: None (limit present)
options: Motor noise (~250 Hz) gets through the filters, and the RPM filter is not working — there is no eRPM telemetry
The 250 Hz peak is a frame resonance; the RPM filter will not help here, only a static notch is needed
The filters are too strong: 4 dB of attenuation means an over-filtered gyro, they have to be loosened
The gyro is damaged: 13 °/s of noise after the filters is impossible on a healthy sensor
questions.explain: A peak at the motor frequency, weak attenuation and the absence of eRPM point to an RPM filter that is not working.
